sections.problem: In this fictional scenario, volunteers maintain a shared garden. Tasks are scattered across messages, so volunteers repeat finished work or overlook work with no owner.
sections.users: Garden volunteers who create, claim and complete tasks on a shared board.
sections.outcomes: Volunteers can see open tasks, identify the owner and read what was done. These are intended outcomes, not measured results.
sections.useCases:
UC-01: A volunteer creates and assigns a task.
UC-02: A volunteer completes or reopens a task.
UC-03: A volunteer filters tasks assigned to them.
sections.scope: One fictional garden board. Include task creation, one owner per task, completion notes, reopening and task filters.
sections.nonGoals: Recurring tasks, calendar sync, payments, real member profiles, public sharing and photo uploads.
sections.inputsOutputs: Inputs: task title, optional due date, selected owner and completion note. Outputs: an open or completed task, its history and a filtered task list.

requirements.outcome: The group can record work that needs doing.
requirements.behavior: Let a volunteer create a task with a title and optional due date.
requirements.acceptance: A nonempty title creates one open task. A blank title is rejected with a visible message. Reopening the board shows the saved task.

requirements.outcome: The group knows who is responsible.
requirements.behavior: Let a volunteer assign or change a task’s owner.
requirements.acceptance: A task shows one selected owner or Unassigned. Changing the owner replaces the assignment without creating a second task.

requirements.outcome: Other volunteers can understand what was completed.
requirements.behavior: Require a completion note when a volunteer marks a task done.
requirements.acceptance: A task with a nonempty completion note can be marked done. Without a note, it remains open and shows a validation message. The saved note remains readable.

requirements.outcome: The group can resume work without losing the earlier record.
requirements.behavior: Let a volunteer reopen a completed task while keeping its earlier completion note.
requirements.acceptance: Reopening changes the task to open. The previous completion note remains available in its history.

requirements.outcome: Volunteers can find their own work.
requirements.behavior: Let a volunteer filter the board to tasks assigned to them.
requirements.acceptance: The My tasks filter shows only tasks assigned to the current volunteer. The All tasks filter restores the full list. Neither filter changes a task or its owner.

sections.quality: Task changes and history must survive reopening the board. Labels and actions must be usable with a keyboard. A failed save must keep the draft available for another attempt.
sections.metrics: Proposed measures: tasks with an owner and completed tasks with a readable note. No adoption measurements or real outcomes exist for this mock example.
sections.risks: The demonstration covers the listed requirements only. It does not establish performance under load, real volunteer adoption or readiness for deployment.
sections.decisions: No open decision blocks these five mock requirements. Recurring tasks and photo uploads remain outside this scope.
sections.evidence: This PRD is entirely fictional. Its review verdicts, proof and attachments are simulated examples. No real product, user research or test result is represented.
